title: Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning Operations Technician
raw_text:
8-490B. Military Occupational Specialty 490B – Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning
Operations Technician (Effective 202610)
    a. Licensing/certification requirement. NA.
    b. Prerequisites. DA Pam 611-21.
    c. MOS 490B. MOS 490B is an accession MOS. The enlisted feeder MOS is any MOS.
    Candidates must possess the following qualifications.
         (a) Must be SGT (E-5) or Above
         (b) Must have completed Warrior Leaders Course (WLC)
         (b) Must meet all Administrative Requirements to become a Warrant Officer.
                    • Be a U.S. citizen (No waivers)
                    • Possess a SECRET with eligibility to obtain TOP SECRET (No waivers)
                    • ASVAB GT Score of 110 (No waivers)
                    • High-School Graduate or GED (No waivers)
                    • Pass Commissioning Physical
    d. Associated SQI.
         (1) 0--No special qualifications.
         (2) 8--Instructor.
         (3) P--Parachutist.
         (4) Z--Research, Development, Test, and Evaluation Technician.
    e. Associated ASI.
         2V: Artificial Intelligence Technician
        Note: Refer to table 6-6 for (Listing of universal ASI’s associated with all warrant officer
        MOS)).
    f. Qualifications.
         (1) All applicants must apply, be accepted, and graduate from the Army’s Artificial
Intelligence Technician Training Program (AITP). Additionally, applicants must be fulfilling, or
have completed, the AITP two-year utilization within the Army’s Artificial Intelligence Integration
Center.
         (2) WO1/CW2 must--
               (a) Be a U.S. citizen. Possess a TOP SECRET security clearance with eligibility for
access to sensitive compartmented information (SCI).
               (b) Complete 490B Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning (AI/ML) Operations
                   Technician Warrant Officer Basic Course.
               (c) Possess a 490B Additional Skill Identifier (ASI)
                     • 2V: AI Technician
               (d) Upon completion of 490B AI/ML Operations Technician Warrant Officer Basic
Course, WOs incur a 6-year term of service obligation.
         (3) CW3 must—
                    (a) Meet qualifications described in paragraph f (2).
                    (b) Complete the Warrant Officer Advanced Common Core.
                    (c) Complete 490B AI/ML Operations Technician Warrant Officer Advanced
Course.
         (4) CW4 must—
                    (a) Meet qualifications described in paragraph f (3).
                    (b) Complete the Warrant Officer Intermediate Level Education (WOILE).
         (5) CW5 must—
                    (a) Meet qualifications described in paragraph f (4).
                    (b) Complete the Warrant Officer Senior Service Education (WOSSE).
g. Duties.
    (1) WO1/CW2 must-
        (a) A Basic-level AI/ML Operations Technician applies fundamental skills of cloud native
software development, data engineering, DevSecOps, AI model deployment, and computer
scripting languages to facilitate AI solution development. Monitor, test, deploy, orchestrate, and
maintain the development of AI solutions. Collaborate with Cyber and Signal team members to
integrate appropriate security features, articulate network requirements, complete necessary
documentation and diagrams to enable AI solution deployment onto Department of Defense
Information Networks.
        (b) Integrate into a multi-disciplined team comprised of Software, Cyber, Signal, and
Operational Research and Systems Analysis (ORSA) personnel.
          (c) Complete assigned tasks and modules, as required and assigned by a Senior- or
Master-level level AI/ML Operations Technician.
      (2) CW3 must--
         (a) Perform duties described in paragraph g (1).
         (b) An Advanced-level AI/ML Operations Technician leverages Lean and Agile
methodologies and management practices to lead AI-focused development projects.
Collaborates with software, Cyber, Signal, and ORSA teams to determine organizational
requirements and design feasible and maintainable solutions to address gaps. Integrates
new practices or technologies into current operations. Provides training, direction, and
oversight to Basic-level AI/ML Operations Technicians. Provides mentorship and talent
management for career progression of Junior Warrant Officers.
         (c) An Advanced-level AI/ML Operations Technician is responsible for completing
assigned tasks and modules, as required and assigned by a Senior-level AI/ML Operations
Technician.
     (3) CW4 must--
         (a) Perform duties described in paragraph g (1 & 2).
         (b) A Senior-level AI/ML Operations Technician possesses skills in negotiation, policy
             analysis, and development. Can demonstrate knowledge in force management and
             emerging technologies.
         (c) Serves as a principal advisor to decision- and policy makers on AI/ML Operations
             training, policies, procedures, and best practices for AI capability development and
             deployment. Responsible for collaborating on operational and strategic-level solutions.
         (d) Set conditions for training and mentorship of Basic and Advanced AI/ML Technicians.
             Reinforce training carrier progression opportunities and cross-functional collaboration to
             share best practices.
    (4) CW5 must--
         (a) Perform duties described in paragraph g (1, 2, & 3).
         (b) Deliver master-level technical and tactical expertise on the primary duties of technical
leader, manager, multidiscipline AI/ML integrator, and advisor.
         (c) Provide direction, guidance, resources, assistance, and supervision necessary for
subordinates to perform their duties.
         (d) Support commanders with the development of new AI/ML Operations doctrine,
organizational structure, methods and equipment to be utilized by AI/ML Operations
Technicians.
         (e) Provide leader development, talent and lifecycle management, mentorship, advice, and
counsel to enlisted Soldiers, warrant officers, and branch officers.
         (f) Possess special leadership abilities that interprets the commander’s intent and mission
to support Multi-Domain Operations (MDO), representing and advising on the responsibilities of
AI/ML Operations within their respective AOR.
         (g) Primarily support corps, echelons above corps, major command, Joint, Interagency,
Intergovernmental, and Multinational operations.
h. Physical demands category, grading, and position titles.
    (1) Physical Demands Category (PDC) – Moderately Heavy.
    (2) Meet physical standards per AR 40-501, chapter 2.
    (3) Have 20/40 correctable vision per AR 40-501, paragraphs 2-13 and 5-17 and meet hearing
standards of AR 40-501, paragraphs 2-7 and 5-18.
    (4) Table 8-280A-1. Physical requirements.
    (a) A minimum OPAT score of Standing Long Jump (LJ) – 0120 cm, seated Power Throw (PT)
– 0350 cm, Strength Deadlift (SD) – 0120 lbs., and Interval Aerobic Run (IR) – 0036 shuttles
Physical Demand Category in “Moderate” (Gold).
     (5) The following grades are used to code positions into one of four definable skill levels: W2
equals WO1/CW2; W3 equals CW3; W4 equals CW4; and W5 equals CW5. The grades are
listed in the following standards of grade tables: Table 8-280A-3. Standards of grade TDA.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
